acceptance.sourceAssertion: Given real dashboard subprocesses in separate temporary profile scopes and registered OS save failures, When public scoped auth flows run, Then only the active profile changes, fresh-process usability agrees and save failure returns sanitized 400 with no success claim/token.

existingDashboardPreparation.preparedBehavior: The existing patch sanitizes dashboard OAuth AuthError/OSError failures and maps OS save errors to HTTP 400; it already applies to the pinned source. No runtime or assigned-AT proof exists.

sourceBoundDiagnosis.sourceSupportedRoute: The pinned public `hermes dashboard` command starts the real server. The existing public POST /api/providers/oauth/openai-codex/start?profile=<name> starts a fixed device-code flow; GET /api/providers/oauth/openai-codex/poll/<session_id>?profile=<name> reads its result. The session captures the selected profile and the worker saves inside that profile scope. A profile-scoped OSError is recorded as an error with status 400 and the poll route returns a fixed sanitized message.
sourceBoundDiagnosis.smallestGap: AT90 is not registered or dispatched. HermesAuthProbe and runHermesAuthFixture currently drive auth CLI operations only; the external fake dispatches add phases to auth add and its EIO hook targets HERMES_HOME/auth.json. They do not launch a dashboard subprocess, drive its public OAuth routes, or target a profile auth.json.
sourceBoundDiagnosis.minimalSeam: Extend the existing HermesAuthProbe/auth-fixture owner and external auth fixture only. Apply the already-prepared dashboard patch to the isolated pinned candidate; launch the pinned public dashboard in temporary HOME with loopback host, port 0, no browser, and isolated mode; drive its existing profile-scoped start/poll routes over loopback with a synthetic ephemeral session token. Extend the existing fake OAuth/OS seam to dispatch the dashboard flow and target the one designated temporary profile store for the existing atomic-replace EIO fault. No new server, endpoint, provider, DTO, or product protocol.

sourceBindings.finding: Unfiltered auth IDs and fixture dispatch currently stop at AT89; there is no AT90 manifest guard or dashboard-scope dispatch.
The existing owner pins and patches a disposable candidate, launches fresh public Hermes commands with bounded children, and has reusable process control; it has no dashboard server/HTTP driver.

Already maps OAuth worker AuthError/OSError to a generic session error status 400 and returns a fixed sanitized 400 from public poll; start also sanitizes AuthError/OSError. No product patch extension is indicated before runtime evidence.
The pinned route API accepts a profile query, worker stores the profile with the OAuth session and scopes the token save to it; the prepared patch sanitizes OSError handling.
The public dashboard CLI accepts loopback host, port 0, --no-open, --isolated and --skip-build, so the test can avoid installed services and browser/build side effects.
A synthetic HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN is accepted through X-Hermes-Session-Token on loopback; only the temporary test token is used and no token is written to evidence.

Existing fake returns fixed Codex device-code, poll and token responses and has an EIO os.rename fault after token response; its dispatch targets CLI auth-add and root HERMES_HOME/auth.json only. Extend these same seams to the dashboard process and its selected profile store.
AT84 already registers profile-auth-atomic-replace-eio as an OS fault. Reuse its mechanism for AT90's single save-failure profile and bind the AT90 phase explicitly.
Existing profile persistence ADR establishes scoped temporary profile stores; the AT90 probe should add one written test-owner interface, not a new auth module.

writtenInterfaceFirst.decision: Extend HermesAuthProbe.run and runHermesAuthFixture with a closed dashboard-scope mode. Keep the existing CheckViewV1 evidence, public OAuth HTTP routes, pinned Hermes child, and fixed external fake OAuth/model/OS seams; add no DTO, module, route, endpoint, provider, or runtime.

temporarySetup: Within one new private test home, create `success` and `toy` profiles via pinned public profile commands and set their Codex provider config through the public CLI; take root, success-profile, and toy-profile auth digests after setup.

Run one pinned `hermes dashboard --host 127.0.0.1 --port 0 --no-open --isolated --skip-build` subprocess per profile scope, sequentially, with the same temporary HERMES_HOME and only loopback HTTP. The public profile query selects the scope; no installed dashboard/service or browser is contacted.

Use an ephemeral synthetic HERMES_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TOKEN via X-Hermes-Session-Token for the start route. Keep session IDs and token material in process memory; receipts retain only digests and sanitized response facts.

mandatoryCases.oracle: The fixed fake device flow reaches approved; only profiles/success/auth.json changes, while profiles/toy/auth.json and root auth remain unchanged. Record exact fake request ledger and no denials/token output.

operations: Fresh pinned `hermes --profile success auth list openai-codex`
Fresh pinned `hermes --profile success chat --provider openai-codex --model gpt-6.1-sol --toolsets none -q <fixed prompt>`
mandatoryCases.oracle: The saved row is readable and a new process obtains the expected fake model response/generation. Root and toy-profile auth digests remain stable. No fallback or denied HTTP request.

operations: Fresh pinned `hermes --profile toy auth list openai-codex`
mandatoryCases.oracle: After the fixed fake token exchange, trigger the existing profile-auth-atomic-replace-eio OS control on profiles/toy/auth.json. Require poll HTTP 400 with the fixed sanitized detail, no success/approved claim, no token or raw exception in response/evidence, and an empty fresh list. Root and success-profile auth digests remain unchanged; the failed profile auth digest remains absent or byte-identical to its pre-flow value.
